# Chapter I - Governance {#c1}

## A. Board Oversight {#a}

1. Every bank shall put in place a Board-approved policy on fraud risk management, which shall be reviewed at least once in three years.

2. The Board shall constitute a Special Committee of the Board for Monitoring and Follow-up of Cases of Frauds, chaired by a whole-time director, with at least two independent directors as members.

# Chapter II - Early Warning Signals {#c2}

## B. Early Warning Signals and Red Flagged Accounts {#b}

3. Banks shall put in place a framework for Early Warning Signals for detection of fraudulent activities and shall examine accounts showing such signals for possible classification as Red Flagged Accounts.

4. A bank shall complete the examination of a Red Flagged Account and decide whether it is a fraud within a maximum period of one hundred and eighty days from the date of red flagging.

# Chapter III - Reporting {#c3}

## C. Reporting Timelines {#c}

5. Banks shall report frauds to the supervisor within the timelines and to the authorities set out in the table below.

| Amount involved | Report to | Timeline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Less than rupees one lakh | Supervisor, through the fraud reporting module | Within 14 days of classification |
| Rupees one lakh and above but less than rupees three crore | Supervisor and local police | Within 7 days of classification |
| Rupees three crore and above | Supervisor, local police and the central investigation agency | Within 7 days of classification |

6. Cases of attempted fraud involving rupees fifty crore or more shall be reported to the Special Committee of the Board.
